decisions.subject: Project engine baseline
decisions.question: Which engine baseline should this implementation use?
decisions.decision: Update the project across the board to the latest stable Godot. Official latest-stable verification is recorded separately in the project baseline.

decisions.subject: Development planning priority
decisions.question: How important is job-game takeover readiness for planning?
decisions.decision: Job-game takeover readiness (MA-DOC-006) is critical to the owner and comes first in development planning; it does not reorder the child-facing defect repairs.
decisions.note: Owner, 2026-09-30: the purpose is to take over development of Mermaid Roshan, and including this in the audit is critical. Recorded the same day in master audit section 13 as 'critical to the owner and comes first in development planning'; that line moved to the baseline history on 2026-10-03 without a register entry, so the roadmap lost it. Entered 2026-10-03 by Claude from those two sources; no new owner answer is claimed.

decisions.subject: Chef look and pour (owner acceptance, DL-QA-06)
decisions.question: Does the Chef job look and pour right in the current build?
decisions.decision: No. Owner, 2026-10-03: "Chef pours backwards still" and "Chef still looks bad, lots of overdraw". Chef's look and pour are not accepted.
decisions.note: The pour direction becomes checkable once Codex adds the CR0 probe assertion (stream starts at the rendered spout; spout lowest at full tilt); the look stays an owner judgement.

decisions.subject: Animation production methods
decisions.decision: Allow final animation workflows with identity, motion, provenance and device checks; replace compulsory individually generated still frames for new authorized production.
decisions.question: Final animation workflows

decisions.subject: Animation cleanup
decisions.decision: Use Aseprite as the bridge when possible to clean results, preserving approved polished 2D identity.
decisions.question: Aseprite bridge

decisions.subject: Animation production routing
decisions.decision: Default local setup for character design/animation and objects, with APIs for cinematic scenes. This preference does not commission character redesign, a 3D medium change, paid jobs or installation of every candidate.
decisions.question: Local versus API

decisions.subject: Roshan sprite orientation
decisions.question: Q1: is left and right only still the standard for gameplay swimming?
decisions.decision: Sprites need left and right orientation only, with no up or down orientation; standard swimming uses left and right views (confirms the 2026-09-16 two-view swim direction).

decisions.subject: Roshan animation production workflow
decisions.question: Q3: V1 or V2 shot card?
decisions.decision: Production runs through LTX locally, by a script run by Codex, with frames transferred through Aseprite for in-game use. Grok handoffs and shot cards are test documents digested to examine the workflow, not final references; the owner assumes V2 is higher quality and asked for an audit.

decisions.subject: Roshan animation scope
decisions.question: Q4: may gameplay animation be painted limited animation?
decisions.decision: No limited animation: make a rich, comprehensive set of Roshan animations. Develop test animations, workflow and style first, then analyse every room and game for right and wrong animations, then polish and refine the product.

decisions.subject: Sky Lagoon travel
decisions.question: Q5: how does Roshan travel on land in the Sky Lagoon?
decisions.decision: In the Sky Lagoon Roshan still swims, with a different animation from the sea: slower, more modest travel.

decisions.subject: Roshan animation template
decisions.question: Goal statement, with Q6 on the uncommitted strict-rule note
decisions.decision: Goal: a template for developing all future Roshan animations from the game and its context; the handoff analyses each scene and Roshan's interactions, decides whether an animation should be generated and hands it to the appropriate model. The uncommitted strict-rule note is a work-in-progress rule; this process describes the workflow.

decisions.subject: Roshan character animation: whole-figure frames
decisions.question: Review of the 2D-deformation wave (revision 1), where a cut-out arm moved over a body taken from another drawing with per-part delays.
decisions.decision: Rejected: "No arm moves as a single figure, the whole body moves at once, drawn as a whole frame." No limb moves as a separate piece; every frame is one whole drawing of the figure and the whole body moves together.
